body.statement: Uniformly over \(P\in\mathcal P_n(a,b,c)\) when \((a,b,c)\) ranges over a compact subset of \([1/2,1]\times(0,1]\times[0,1]\), the complete aggregate tangent weights implied by incoherence and the two normalized restricted-Gram bounds satisfy \(s^{-2}\sum_{j\in I,s'\in J}w_{js'}^2=O(1)\) and \(s^{-1}\max_{j\in I,s'\in J}|w_{js'}|=o(1)\).
body.justification: The frontier weighted-Lindeberg bounds must adapt to both the treated-pre and donor-window variance components as \(b\) and \(c\) vary.
body.gap: No checked weak-factor result derives score diffuseness uniformly over a three-exponent deterministic block-missing class.
body.consumer: The frontier central limit theorem uses these bounds without fixing the cohort exponent at one.
body.proof_tex:
The normalized-factor argument in the proof of \(\mathrm{lem:score\mbox{-}diffuseness}\) uses only balanced growth, incoherence, and the two restricted-Gram bounds.  It therefore gives uniformly on every compact exponent set
\[
 |a_{ij,t}|\le Cn^{-1},
 \qquad |b_{t,s}|\le Cn^{-1}.
\]
With \(g\asymp n^b\) and \(H\asymp n^c\), expansion of the three-term score gives
\[
 \max_{j,s'}|w_{js'}|
 \le C\max\left\{\frac1{nH},\frac1{ng},\frac1{n^2}\right\}
\]
and, by counting the same three disjoint supports,
\[
 \sum_{j,s'}w_{js'}^2
 \le C\left\{\frac1{nH}+\frac1{ng}+\frac1{n^2}\right\}.
\]
The frontier variance lower bound is
\[
 s^2\ge c_v\left\{\frac1{nH}+\frac1{ng}\right\},
\]
so the squared-weight sum divided by \(s^2\) is uniformly bounded.  Each component of the maximum is negligible relative to \(s\):
\[
 \frac{(nH)^{-1}}{s}\le\frac1{\sqrt{nH}},
 \qquad
 \frac{(ng)^{-1}}{s}\le\frac1{\sqrt{ng}},
 \qquad
 \frac{n^{-2}}{s}\le \frac{\sqrt{nH}}{n^2}+\frac{\sqrt{ng}}{n^2}.
\]
On a compact subset of \([1/2,1]\times(0,1]\times[0,1]\), the exponent \(b\) is bounded below by a positive constant, while \(c\ge0\).  Thus \(nH\to\infty\), \(ng\to\infty\), and every right-hand side tends to zero uniformly.  This proves the frontier diffuseness claims.
